Package org.aeonbits.owner.loaders

Class XMLLoader

java.lang.Object
org.aeonbits.owner.loaders.XMLLoader
All Implemented Interfaces:
Serializable, Loader
public class XMLLoader extends Object implements Loader
A loader able to read properties from standard XML Java properties files, as well as user defined XML properties files.

1.0.5

    • load

      public void load(Properties result, URI uri) throws IOException
      Reads the document, holding it to the grammar it declares.

      A document carrying a DOCTYPE is validated against it and a violation is refused, which is what the JDK does for its own properties format and what Commons Configuration does when asked to validate at all. A document declaring no grammar is read as it is; there is nothing to hold it to.

      #validate=false on the source turns that off — file:app.xml#validate=false — and the document is then read whatever its own grammar says of it. It is worth having for a file that is out of step with a DTD nobody maintains any more, and it is written on the source rather than configured globally because it is a property of that file and not of the application.

      Specified by:
      load in interface Loader
      Parameters:
      result - the resulting properties where to load the uri
      uri - the URI from where to load the properties.
      Throws:
      IOException - if there is some I/O error during the load.

    • defaultSpecFor

      public String defaultSpecFor(String urlPrefix)
      Description copied from interface: Loader
      Returns the default URI specification for a given URI resource, that can be handled by this loader.

      Returning null means this loader adds nothing to the sources looked for in the absence of @Sources - which is what SystemLoader and DotEnvLoader both do, since neither is named after the configuration interface. That is also why this method has a default: it is a choice a loader is allowed to decline, and declining it should not require writing a method that returns nothing.

      A loader offering more than one name - a format spelled .yaml and .yml, or .ini and .cfg - overrides Loader.defaultSpecsFor(String) instead. The two are not meant to be overridden together.

      Specified by:
      defaultSpecFor in interface Loader
      Parameters:
      urlPrefix - the prefix identifying the URI resource.
      Returns:
      the default URI specification for a given URI resource, or null for none.
